description: Seven-note arpeggiator with sixteen patterns, three sub-steps per note, note lengths from a whole note down to a thirty-second, and glide and legato per note

inputs.text: The clock the arpeggio runs from; with nothing patched here the trigger output stays at 0V and the pattern does not advance
Adds its voltage to the pitch output, transposing the arpeggio
A rising edge here queues the next pattern, which takes effect at the start of the next pass
A rising edge here restarts the pattern at its first note

outputs.text: A 10V gate for as long as the current note lasts, dropped one tick early so consecutive notes do not run together
The pitch of the current note, a volt per octave, with the pattern's octave setting and the V/OCT offset input added, and sliding over 200ms on a note marked for glide

notes: the module plays nothing until a clock is patched to Clk, at least one note on the keyboard is on, and at least one of that note's three sub-steps is set to Note
every sub-step of a new module is set to Off and no key is on, which is why a freshly added module is silent under a running clock
clicking a key on the keyboard adds that note to the arpeggio and clicking it again removes it; seven notes can be on at once
the upper row of marks above the Pattern strip sets the last pattern in the run, and the lower row picks which pattern is shown

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.3: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
